html:
The Kingdom of León was a Christian kingdom in north-west Spain, from 910 to 1230. It grew out of the Kingdom of Asturias when the kings moved their seat south from the mountains to the city of León. On the map for 1000 to 1200 it stretches from Galicia to the Duero.

For its first century it was the leading Christian power facing al-Andalus in the Reconquista, and its kings sometimes called themselves emperor. Its eastern frontier county, Castile, broke away and soon outgrew it. Under Alfonso VI, king of both, the Christians took Toledo in 1085. The pilgrim road of the Camino de Santiago ran across the kingdom.

The Cortes of León of 1188, where townsmen sat beside nobles and clergy, is often called the earliest European parliament with town representatives. In 1230 Ferdinand III inherited León and joined it to Castile for good, forming the Crown of Castile.
